scene_reference.setting: Snowbound 1870s mountain outpost interior (haberdashery‑like cabin), mid‑day blizzard outside.
scene_reference.note: This is an homage micro‑sequence designed to evoke the film’s look without reproducing a specific shot or dialogue.

capture_format.justification: Ultra Panavision 70 with a projected 2.76:1 image is the hallmark format associated with the production.

cameras_lenses.camera_body_emulation: Panavision System 65 Studio / HS (spinning mirror reflex)
cameras_lenses.lens_character: Gentle focus roll‑off and ‘dappled, impressionistic’ depth cues from vintage Ultra Panavision optics; minimal diffusion in front of lens.

stocks_color.processing_note: Interiors commonly ride at 500 ASA; modest push was sometimes used.

air_conditions.reason: Visible breath plumes; production famously chilled interiors to ~30°F with high humidity.

environmental_fx.atmosphere: Light haze for volumetric shafts and lamp halation (do not obscure faces).
environmental_fx.exterior: Continuous snow with gusts visible through windows; wind‑driven snow machines outside.

sound_bed_guidance: Low, constant blizzard rumble; intermittent wood creaks; quiet stovepipe tick; distant horse jostle muffled.

set_layout.units: meters (origin at center of main table)

subject_A.desc: Coat‑clad traveler with brimmed hat; seated left of table

subject_B.desc: Badge‑wearing figure; standing by post near window

lighting_rig.color_policy: Warm interior tungsten (key 3000–3200K) vs cold exterior daylight (5600K) for contrast.

fixtures.aim: Edge light on Subject B’s shoulder/hat

fixtures.mods: 12x12 216 diffusion + Full CTB + snow/rain bars + wind fan
fixtures.note: Creates blue‑white back edge and visible snow gusts

fixtures.aim: Increase contrast on Subject A’s camera‑left cheek

timeline_seconds.framing: Ultra‑wide two‑shot: Subject A left third at table, Subject B right third near window; door and stove as deep background anchors.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: Hold base plan; practical lamps at 80% to bloom slightly.
timeline_seconds.texture_fx: Light haze; breath plumes faint; snow visible through window.
timeline_seconds.sound_cues: Muffled wind bed; distant door rattle once.

camera.move: begin 0.25 m dolly push‑in on table axis (0.25 m/s)
camera.focus_pull: micro‑adjust to 2.8 m as parallax changes

timeline_seconds.framing: Foreground coffee steam curls into top light; Subjects’ hat brims touch top frame line for tension.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: Nudge KEY_R dimmer +0.1 stop to keep faces at T2.8 as camera advances.
timeline_seconds.texture_fx: Steam and breath intermingle; a spark pops in stove (subtle light kick).

timeline_seconds.framing: Window brightens with a gust; elongated anamorphic bokeh in background.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: WINDOW_DAY gust raises level +0.3 stop for one second (fan burst).
timeline_seconds.texture_fx: Breath plume from Subject B crosses frame right‑to‑left.

camera.move: finalize push‑in (total 0.75 m since start); slight 0.5° tilt up to catch eyes under brims

timeline_seconds.framing: Tension beat: Subjects hold eye‑line offscreen; lamp halation kisses lens.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: Introduce -0.2 stop on TOP_BOX to deepen hat shadows; maintain FILL_L_BOUNCE at -1.5 stops.

camera.focus_pull: rack 2.4 m → 3.4 m to window post (Subject B) over 0.6 s

timeline_seconds.framing: Momentary emphasis on Subject B silhouette and snow vortices.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: BACK_RIM edges B’s hat; allow slight flare streak.

timeline_seconds.edit: CUT to medium close‑up on Subject A
timeline_seconds.framing: MCU from chest up; nose at left third; empty space to the right carries offscreen threat.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: KEY_R flags tightened (add 4" cutter) to sharpen cheek falloff; practical lamp glows in bokeh.
timeline_seconds.texture_fx: Breath condenses; micro‑beads on moustache; coffee steam rises between lens and subject.

camera.focus_pull: subtle 1.2 m → 1.15 m to catch eye sparkle

timeline_seconds.framing: Eye highlight from FILL_L_BOUNCE; brim shadow just kisses brow.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: Dim PRACTICALS −5% to settle flare; increase NEG_FILL proximity by 10 cm to deepen contrast.

timeline_seconds.framing: Stillness; breath plume exits frame as wind thuds against door offscreen.
timeline_seconds.lighting_changes: WINDOW_DAY drops back to base; TOP_BOX pulses +0.1 stop (stove tick) for a naturalistic shimmer.
timeline_seconds.sound_cues: One wood‑beam groan; blizzard rumble rises 1 dB and settles.

subject_A.wardrobe: Dark wool coat with fur collar; black felt hat; leather gloves; scarf frost at edges.
subject_A.props: Tin coffee cup; oil lamp at elbow; revolver holster stays holstered.

subject_B.wardrobe: Heavy duster; sheriff’s star; scarf; snowflake flecks on shoulder from recent entry.
subject_B.props: Gloved hand on post; breath visible when turning toward window.

post_pipeline.scan_emulation: Grain: fine 65mm pattern (luma 20%, chroma 12%); gate weave 0.1px random; tiny dust motes occasionally glint in top light.

color_pipeline.contrast: medium‑high; protect lamp highlights; cyan‑leaning shadows from window light

post_pipeline.audio_mix: Blizzard -22 LUFS integrated; room tone creaks -28 LUFS; cup set‑down -26 LUFS; no score, or single held bass note -30 LUFS.

direction_notes: Maintain long‑take tension even across the cut by matching head position and breath rhythm.
Keep faces readable under hat brims via low, warm fill while preserving strong top‑shadow character.
Let practical‑lamp halation and vintage‑lens aberrations provide organic softness; avoid modern diffusion.
safety_and_attribution: Format, aspect ratio, lens family, and stock references reflect public reporting about the production’s use of Ultra Panavision 70 on 65mm with specific Kodak Vision3 stocks.
Interior climate details (≈30°F, 80% humidity) are drawn from American Cinematographer’s set coverage.
Interiors operating around 500 ASA and the general 70mm ‘roadshow’ context are documented in trade coverage.
sources: American Cinematographer – “Wide Wide West: The Hateful Eight” (format, stocks, set climate, lens characteristics).
Wired – on the 70mm roadshow engagement and Ultra Panavision 70 (context, aspect ratio).
Variety – Robert Richardson comments on interior stock speed (500 ASA).
